Apple recently replaced a billboard in Milan that originally featured a toddler holding an iPhone, as part of its latest "Relax, it's iPhone" advertising campaign. Details below.

Apple removes controversial Italian billboard

A few days ago, Italy's child rights watchdog, the Autorità Garante per l'Infanzia e l'Adolescenza (AGIA), publicly condemned Apple for depicting a young child holding an iPhone in its "Relax, it's iPhone" advertising campaign.

The campaign highlights the durability and sturdiness of the iPhone, showing scenarios where the device gets wet, dropped, or otherwise used in ways that could potentially damage it — including someone taking photos in heavy rain, someone watching videos with the iPhone on the edge of a bathtub, a dog chewing on an iPhone, and a toddler clumsily holding the device.

As soon as the billboard depicting this last scenario was erected on via Melchiorre Gioia in Milan, AGIA received a complaint letter from a member of the public, accusing the advertisement of normalising "electronic babysitter" behaviour.

AGIA expressed agreement and forwarded the case to Italy's communications regulator AGCOM, the Italian Competition Authority AGCM, and the local advertising industry self-regulatory body IAP, "for appropriate review and any possible action."

According to reports by Prima Comunicazione and Repubblica Milano, Apple has removed the controversial billboard and replaced it with one promoting the Find My feature.

Apple has not publicly responded to the incident, but the company's swift action reflects that it takes the criticism seriously — even though the original intent of the ad was to showcase the iPhone's durability, external interpretations have differed.

What are your thoughts on this controversy? Feel free to share them in the comments section.
